01 — THE OBSESSION

M/S Drotten is the best ship.
Here are the numbers to back me up.

M/S Drotten is the best ship because somebody put 50,400 kW of machinery inside a 196-metre passenger ferry and I apparently need an entire website to explain how much I love that. She does 28.5 knots. That’s about 52.8 km/h. Look at her SIZE and then think about that speed again.

This is my Drotten site. The specification list is compulsory. scroll slowly.

Actual ship numbers ↗

03 — MY FAVOURITE BIT

FOUR.
WÄRTSILÄ.
ENGINES.

4 × WÄRTSILÄ 12V46C
50,400kW OF MAIN MACHINERY

Wärtsilä 46-series diesels. Wärtsilä supplied eight main engines across the two sister ships.

Drotten’s exact engine listing: four Wärtsilä 12V46C engines. Four. I could have put this beside the power figure but then you might have scrolled past it.

04 — SAME SHIP, EARLIER NAME
2003 — 2020M/S GOTLAND↓2020 —M/S DROTTENIMO 9223796. That’s her.

THE GOTLAND
NAME THING.

Drotten was M/S Gotland from 2003 to 2020, so finding an old photo with GOTLAND on her is like finding another bit of her photo album. I will open one picture to check the name and suddenly there are fourteen tabs and it’s late.

Same ship, earlier name, years of crossings already behind her. This is why I care about IMO 9223796 so much: names move around, and I want to know which actual hull I’m looking at.

The 2003 Gotland became Drotten in 2020. I keep both names in my searches because otherwise you miss SEVENTEEN YEARS of her history.
